reason: The cited evidence does not address thermally activated phase transformations, Mg depletion, or oxide scale evolution in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs. E1 and E2 discuss corrosion mechanisms in Mg-Ti-Zn alloys, while E3 provides general thermodynamic principles of selective oxidation, but none support the specific mechanistic chain proposed.
premises: Thermally activated phase transformations in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs cause selective intermetallic precipitation and local Mg depletion
Mg depletion alters chemical activity at the oxide/alloy interface during high-temperature oxidation
Altered interface activity shifts the oxide scale from MgO-based to a mixed oxide enriched in protective species like Al2O3
This shift improves corrosion resistance and oxidation behavior compared to the as-cast baseline
